finalAssistantText: {"summary":"Cycle-14 proposal is largely directionally sound for the stated failures. The July proposal correctly keeps the Whipped cod roe false pass classified as source_text (delivery-assessment.ts:254-302 has no negative AST/BOTH guard; supply.html:185 grants changes_suggested for an established omission), so the new negative-only guard is the right hook and needs to act before the supplied status is trusted. However, two things are reachable and not covered in the JSON plan: (a) the whitelist proposal would parse buyer/rule text, where the deterministic static-markup and source-literal directives are word-bounded and reject near-neighbors such as 'with the label' or 'password field', so a literal 'recognize as source_content' is either dead or would broaden the scope and risk neutralizing the OBSERVATION_REQUIRED login/form veto; the proposal must be routed through an exact directive grammar plus an explicit predicate for static markup. (b) The status/ALL reconciliation only improves the downgrade direction; a false pass defined by an ALL relationship where the model quotes a single positive owner still passes as supported unless a 'these are all' limitation is present. That makes cycle 14 depend on model wording in the limitation rather than on source. A concrete, safer alternative is to ground the ALL/BOTH guard on the directive grammar plus the request's own negative statement, keep the present zero-status-trust false-pass block, and add an owner-coverage witness that surfaces remaining uncertainty only when no limitation acknowledges incomplete coverage. No automatic safe/working claim, no promotion and no acceptance/payment widening is proposed here. The award comparison correctly stays on the primary evidence/clear-rules axis; no opponent performance is asserted. This is an unexecuted static critique (no runtime checks were run).","findings":[{"severity":"P1","file":"scripts/evaluation-results/citation-relations-cycle-14-plan.json","line":32,"title":"Static markup renamed to source_text bypasses the runtime/form veto","evidence":"Line 32 says 'Recognize clearly source-only HTML attribute/control relationships as source_content'. Because line 32 is later fed by delivery-assessment.ts:254 (assessmentEvidenceScope) and then line 258 ('requires_observation' -> insufficient_evidence) or line 260 (otherwise the model status is kept), any criterion that becomes category 'source_text' is no longer internally forced to insufficient evidence. The static-markup family in static-markup-directive.ts (1-35 boundary comments) exists to give that scope. But the delivered matcher lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts uses markupDirective, which is staticMarkupDirective() at lines 3-4, 85, 91 and 93. If line 32 is implemented as a new classifier branch, or by widening the markupDirective predicate to fire on near-neighbor text, the scope-branch that leaves 'requires_observation' at 103-105 does not run for that criterion. The title-driven OBSERVATION_REQUIRED check at 103 also relies on 'withoutWorkingTimeUnits'. The login/form families ('forms?', 'log[- ]?in', 'submi(t|ts|tted|tting|ssion|ssions)') are the ones protected by 107 and 190-191. A model 'supported' answer on these would then survive 260-301 (unless a rule fail, business, exact-copy or label check intervenes), producing a 'supported/working' look on a login/form requirement. That is exactly the source-only promotion boundary that line 32 says it will not cross.","reproduction":"Reasoning trace, not run. Feed a manual-* criterion whose title contains 'Login form' and whose source contains 'input type=password on two named files' (line 26 of the plan), or the plan's own line 26 'static input type password on two named files'. Before the change, assessmentEvidenceScope returns requires_observation through OBSERVATION_REQUIRED at 107 and 190-191, and the item is forced to insufficient_evidence at 258. With line 32 implemented as a classification rule, the criterion reaches the line 260 branch and the model status is kept. The model's citations are validated only as source spans (assessment-citation-catalog.ts:139-145) and exact-copy/label checks do not cover a login flow, so a 'supported' item can be returned for a label such as 'Login'.","suggestion":"Do not add a second generic classifier. Implement line 32 only as a staticMarkupDirective exact-grammar path: add the candidate family to isStaticMarkupDirectiveCandidate, keep the near-neighbors rejected, and run every FINANCIAL_ACTION/CARD_DEBIT_ACTION/RECORD_ACTION/EMAIL_DELIVERY_ACTION and OBSERVATION_REQUIRED veto on the combined title and source. The title itself must be checked, not the remaining text after a repeated markup directive is removed, when the title mentions login/form/submit. Add assertions that a login/form criterion stays 'requires_observation' and that only hard rejection stands."},{"severity":"P1","file":"scripts/evaluation-results/citation-relations-cycle-14-plan.json","line":33,"title":"Negative-only ALL/BOTH guard depends on raw explanation wording and misses a false pass","evidence":"Line 33 downgrades only when two conditions hold: the model's raw status is 'supported', the directive is a source-content positive ALL/BOTH/EACH requirement, and the raw explanation contains an 'explicit source missing-label/tag/field/amount statement'. The actual Whipped cod roe explanation (lines 10-21) does contain such a statement, so the guard would catch this one. But nothing in the proposal handles the near neighbor the request names: an ALL/BOTH relationship where the explanation names a positive owner and stays silent about the other owner, or uses different wording ('does not list', 'absent from'). The existing reconcile instruction at delivery-assessment.ts:186 is prompt text aimed at the model, not a deterministic guard. status/ALL-conjunct reconciliation at line 34 is only a strengthening of the model prompt. The server keeps the model status at 260, and the only structural downgrade is the empty-citation check at 298-301. The known 'false pass' class can therefore return as 'supported' for any phrasing outside the finite phrase list, and the guard's correctness depends on untrusted model wording.","reproduction":"Reasoning trace, not run. Reuse the line 10-21 item but change the explanation to 'Homepage lunch pane shows the GF tag next to Whipped cod roe.' with citations s77/s202/s204. If s204 is the menu.html span without the tag, the raw status 'supported' and an explanation with no negative phrase both match. The guard at line 33 does not fire. Lines 255-301 keep 'supported' (no rule fail, no business/eaxact/label/empty-citation path applies), and the item is returned as supported.","suggestion":"Keep the line-33 heuristic as a phrase-level safety net, but combine it with an owner-coverage witness: when a source-content directive requires ALL/BOTH/EACH relationships, require the cited owner spans (one per page, element or label) to cover every mandated owner. If they do not, downgrade to insufficient_evidence and keep the final citation and explanation in a limitation. For added terms such as 'absent', 'not present', 'without' and 'lacks', extend the finite list. The guard must never turn a pass into changes_suggested or into a 'working' claim, and must never change the citations."},{"severity":"P2","file":"lib/assessment-evidence-scope.ts","line":103,"title":"Line 32 'safe' whitelisting could use the OBSERVATION_REQUIRED title veto to block the static classes whose false abstention it targets","evidence":"Lines 103-105 force a requires_observation due to the observation veto appearing in the title. The request names the static false abstatention classes 'static HTML label for/id pairs' and 'static radio name/value/label' (plan lines 24-25). If the buyer's own title or source names a login screen, sign-in or form, it contains 'form'/'login' and the veto fires. That class is precisely the login/account label pair that the static markup directive describes. The same veto problem applies to line 32's candidate grammar: the static-markup candidate description says it is about login/password fields (plan line 26). If line 32 follows the current markupDirective semantics, the OBSERVATION_REQUIRED title check at 103 can undo the intended reconciliation for exactly these pages. The proposal does not say how static label and radio relations are allowed past the 'form'/'login' /'submit' tokens without making the login form itself source-checkable.","reproduction":"Reasoning trace, not run. A manual-* criterion titled 'Login label for/id pairs are associated' whose source instructs a static label control relationship: assessmentEvidenceScope runs 103 and OBSERVATION_REQUIRED matches 'Login'. The result is still requires_observation and stays insufficient evidence at delivery-assessment.ts:258-260, so the staticMarkupFalseAbstention class is not repaired.","suggestion":"State in the plan that static markup classification must be driven only by an exact staticMarkupDirective grammar, and decide explicitly whether that directive suppresses the OBSERVATION_REQUIRED title veto. If it does, list each veto word (login, form, submit, password) and the associated test. Never let the suppression apply when the requirement asks for behavior or operation (the ACTION_OR_CLAUSE grammar already supports this)."},{"severity":"P2","file":"scripts/evaluation-results/citation-relations-cycle-14-plan.json","line":33,"title":"The plan has no 'observations with no browser' class: 'source missing' may be confused with 'rendered missing'","evidence":"The proposal says the negative guard must 'preserve original quote and limitation' and avoid treating 'no-browser evidence as a contradiction'. That phrase is ambiguous. A model explanation saying 'menu.html lists Whipped cod roe without any dish-tag span' is a source-only statement. A model explanation saying 'no GF tag is displayed/visible on menu.html' is a rendered statement that the citations cannot support (assessment-citation-catalog.ts:83-84, 130-144 only binds spans). Because the guard is keyed on the explanation text, wording such as 'not visible' or 'absent' can be read as a source statement even when it is an overclaim. The plan does not separate these two cases, so the same guard can pass a rendered-absence claim into insufficient_evidence while still carrying unreliable wording, or can skip it. A P3 product-flow risk follows: the explanation preserved in the report would carry an unsupported observation.","reproduction":"Reasoning trace, not run. Feed an item whose explanation is 'Menu page is missing the GF tag' (the exact plan phrase 'missing tag'), cited only to a menu.html span without the tag. It is classed as the plan's explicit negative statement, so it is downgraded to insufficient_evidence. The explanation text arguably overclaims rendered state if read literally, or says nothing about where the tag was looked for. The plan neither flags nor rewrites that wording.","suggestion":"Define the negative statement as source-scoped only: require a subject token plus a source-scoped predicate (no 'displayed', 'visible', 'rendered', 'shows' outside a quoted source string). For rendered-abstention statements, keep insufficient_evidence but add a fixed limitation: the negative is source copy only and was not observed in a browser. Do not rewrite the model quote."},{"severity":"P2","file":"scripts/evaluation-results/citation-relations-cycle-14-plan.json","line":35,"title":"Tavola Updateddaily 'p' decision marked conservative but left without a product-flow confirmation","evidence":"Line 35 says the Tavola Updateddaily exact 'p' is 'conservative unknown under omitted CSS/script uncertainty' and that a check should be reported separately on whether that is the current agreed conservative scope. The plan does not define the buyer-facing outcome if that check finds it is not the agreed scope. Since the change set is now source-side, a criterion in that class could keep insufficient_evidence and be misinterpreted by the buyer as 'missing requirement' (the report has no 'not applicable' state). The plan neither states how the buyer sees the reason nor that this is outside the cycle-14 fix.","reproduction":"Reasoning trace, not run. The saved project summary includes 'Updated daily' copy. Line 35 keeps the scope decision open, so the cycle-14 report may show insufficient_evidence for that criterion while the note says it is conservative. A buyer reading the report sees the abstention without the scope decision, and no item is resolved.","suggestion":"State in the plan that an unconfirmed conservative scope is recorded in a limitation and does not convert into changes_suggested, and that the separate scope decision is required before the known-7 repair is declared complete, or is deferred with an explicit owner. Do not invent a new requirement or accept it on the model's behalf."}]}
